name: Transformer (base/big)
notable_for: Google's 2017 Transformer paper introduced an encoder-decoder design for sequence processing that relies on attention and drops recurrence. Earlier language systems read text one word after another; attention lets every word in a passage weigh every other word at once, so training can be spread across many chips in parallel. GPT-1, BERT and T5, released over the next two years, each built on it.

name: GPT-1
notable_for: GPT-1, released by OpenAI in June 2018 with 117 million parameters (adjustable numbers learned in training), demonstrated that generative pre-training followed by task-specific fine-tuning could improve performance across NLP tasks. It first trained one model to predict the next word on a large body of unlabeled text, then gave it short extra training for each job, such as answering questions or judging sentiment. GPT-2 and GPT-3 kept the pretraining step but learned tasks from examples in the prompt instead of extra training.
verification_note: OpenAI published GPT-1 code and pretrained weights (finetune-transformer-lm repo; later mirrored as openai-gpt on Hugging Face).

name: BERT-Large
notable_for: BERT-Large, released by Google in October 2018 with 340 million parameters and open weights, is a bidirectional Transformer encoder pretrained to represent text using both left and right context. Where GPT-1 read text left to right, BERT learned by filling in masked words using the words on both sides, which suits tasks that judge or label text rather than write it. Its weights were free to download, so others could adapt it to their own labeling tasks with little extra training.

name: Megatron-LM
notable_for: Megatron-LM, from NVIDIA in August 2019, introduced efficient intra-layer tensor parallelism and enabled training an 8.3-billion-parameter transformer on 512 GPUs. Tensor parallelism splits each layer's arithmetic across several graphics chips (GPUs), so one model can exceed any single chip's memory. At 8.3 billion parameters it was more than five times GPT-2's 1.5 billion, released three months later, and Megatron-Turing NLG used its approach at 530 billion two years later.

name: T5-11B
notable_for: T5-11B, released by Google in October 2019 with open weights, is an encoder-decoder language model with 11 billion parameters that frames NLP tasks in a unified text-to-text format. Translation, summarizing and question answering were all posed as 'text in, text out', with short instruction prefixes saying which task was wanted.

name: GPT-2
notable_for: GPT-2, OpenAI's 1.5-billion-parameter language model, was released through a staged process during 2019 and can generate realistic paragraphs of text from short prompts. OpenAI published smaller versions first and its full model last, in November, with code and weights, saying this would help researchers detect machine-written text and noting that GPT-2 could be fine-tuned for misuse. Parameters are adjustable numbers learned in training.

name: Turing-NLG
notable_for: Turing-NLG, released by Microsoft in February 2020, was a 17-billion-parameter Transformer-based language model notable for text generation, question answering, and summarization. Parameters are adjustable numbers learned in training; Microsoft called it, at 17 billion, the largest model ever published, roughly twice NVIDIA's 8.3-billion Megatron-LM from six months earlier. GPT-3, at 175 billion, followed three months later.

name: GPT-3
notable_for: GPT-3, released by OpenAI in May 2020, demonstrated strong few-shot performance across many language tasks at 175 billion parameters. Few-shot means it could pick up new tasks from a handful of examples placed in its prompt, with no extra training. Its 175 billion parameters were ten times Turing-NLG's record from three months earlier, and GPT-3.5, which powers ChatGPT, descends from it.

name: Switch Transformer
notable_for: Google Brain's Switch Transformer, published in January 2021 with open weights, scaled a sparsely activated language model to 1.6 trillion parameters and achieved a 4× pretraining speedup over T5-XXL. Sparse activation means its network is divided into many 'experts' and each word fragment is routed to only one of them, so total parameter count is enormous while computation per word stays modest. Mixtral in 2023 and DeepSeek-V3 in 2024 use the same mixture-of-experts idea.

name: DALL-E
notable_for: DALL-E, announced by OpenAI in January 2021 with 12 billion parameters, generates images from text descriptions and can combine unrelated concepts in plausible ways. OpenAI's launch example was one baby daikon radish in a tutu walking a dog. Text-to-image means users type one sentence and receive one picture to match; Stable Diffusion released downloadable weights for this same task 19 months later.

name: CLIP
notable_for: CLIP, released by OpenAI in January 2021 with open weights, learns visual concepts from image-text pairs and enables zero-shot visual classification using natural-language labels. It was trained to match internet images with text written beside them, so it can be asked 'is this photo of a dog?' without additional training examples. One year later it became one half of DALL-E 2's two-stage pipeline.

name: LaMDA
notable_for: LaMDA, Google's 137-billion-parameter model from May 2021, is a dialog-specialized Transformer language model fine-tuned for safety and factual grounding, with the ability to consult external knowledge sources. Fine-tuning means extra training after its main run, here on conversation transcripts rated by people for safety and accuracy; grounding means it could call search or calculator tools to check claims. It came 18 months before ChatGPT.

name: Codex
notable_for: Codex, released by OpenAI in August 2021 with 12 billion parameters, generates program code from natural-language descriptions and was fine-tuned on publicly available Python code. Fine-tuning means a GPT-3 model was given further training on a narrower body of text, here code from public repositories. It solved over 70% of OpenAI's HumanEval programming problems, against 0% for GPT-3, and the same technology powers GitHub's Copilot coding assistant.

name: Megatron-Turing NLG 530B (MT-NLG)
notable_for: Megatron-Turing NLG 530B, from Microsoft and NVIDIA in October 2021, is a 530-billion-parameter, 105-layer transformer language model trained to perform natural language tasks. Those tasks include completion prediction, reading comprehension, and commonsense reasoning. Parameters are adjustable numbers learned in training; 530 billion was three times GPT-3's count, and Microsoft called it the world's largest generative language model. Training it combined Microsoft's DeepSpeed and NVIDIA's Megatron systems for splitting one model across many graphics chips.

name: Gopher
notable_for: Gopher, DeepMind's 280-billion-parameter language model from December 2021, was evaluated on 152 tasks, setting a new state of the art on 100 of 124 tasks with prior best results. State of the art means best published score on standardized tests. Its paper also found gains from scale largest in reading comprehension and fact-checking and smallest in logical and mathematical reasoning; three months later DeepMind's Chinchilla showed training data, not parameter count, was what limited such models.

name: Chinchilla
notable_for: Chinchilla, from Google DeepMind in March 2022, demonstrated compute-optimal training by using 70 billion parameters and 1.4 trillion tokens to outperform several larger language models, including Gopher at 280 billion. Tokens are word fragments read during training; the finding was that models of the day had too many parameters and too little data for their compute budgets. LLaMA-13B beat GPT-3 at 175 billion one year later by training on more text.

name: PaLM
notable_for: PaLM, released by Google in April 2022, is a 540-billion-parameter language model trained with Pathways that achieved state-of-the-art few-shot performance across hundreds of language tasks. Pathways was Google's system for running one training job across two chip clusters; few-shot means learning tasks from examples in its prompt. PaLM's paper showed chain-of-thought prompting, asking for written-out steps, lifting results on arithmetic and logic.

name: DALL-E 2
notable_for: DALL-E 2, from OpenAI in April 2022 with 3.5 billion parameters, generates realistic images from text prompts and supports image editing features such as inpainting and outpainting. Inpainting replaces one selected part of an image from text instructions; outpainting extends it beyond its original edges. It paired OpenAI's CLIP image-text model with a diffusion decoder, which refines random noise into an image step by step, using under one third of DALL-E's 12 billion parameters.

name: OPT-175B
notable_for: OPT-175B, from Meta AI in May 2022, was one of the first 175-billion-parameter language models made available to the research community. Its pretrained weights and training code were shared for noncommercial research use; weights are trained model files, and GPT-3, of equal size, had no public weights. Outside researchers could now study GPT-3-scale models directly, nine months before Meta's LLaMA.
verification_note: OPT-175B weights were released only on request to researchers under a noncommercial license (smaller OPT sizes were openly downloadable).

name: BLOOM
notable_for: BLOOM, released in July 2022 by BigScience, which gathered over 1,000 researchers, is an openly released multilingual language model covering 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. Its 176 billion parameters made it comparable in size to GPT-3, and it was trained on Jean Zay, one supercomputer south of Paris. Hugging Face called it, at release, the world's largest open multilingual model.

name: Stable Diffusion 1.4
notable_for: Stable Diffusion 1.4, from Stability AI in August 2022, was publicly released with downloadable model weights for generating images from text prompts. Weights are trained model files, so people could download the model and run or modify it on their own computers. DALL-E 2, four months earlier, was offered through OpenAI's service without downloadable weights.

name: Whisper
notable_for: Whisper, released by OpenAI in September 2022 with 1.55 billion parameters, is an open-source multilingual speech recognition model that transcribes audio into text and can translate speech into English. It was trained on 680,000 hours of audio paired with transcripts, and open-source means its code and weights are free to download and run. Multilingual means it handles many spoken languages in one model.

name: GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT)
notable_for: GPT-3.5, released by OpenAI in November 2022, powers the original ChatGPT, a conversational model fine-tuned with supervised learning and reinforcement learning from human feedback. Supervised learning here means training on example conversations written by people; reinforcement learning from human feedback means raters ranked its answers and it was tuned toward the preferred ones. That tuning turned GPT-3's raw text prediction into an assistant that answers follow-up questions, admits mistakes and rejects inappropriate requests.

name: LLaMA
notable_for: LLaMA, from Meta AI in February 2023, came in sizes up to 65 billion parameters, and LLaMA-13B outperformed GPT-3 on most benchmarks despite having far fewer parameters. Benchmarks are standardized tests; its 13-billion version beat GPT-3 at 13 times its size by training on more text, following Chinchilla's 2022 result. Meta granted access to its weights case by case for research; five months later Llama 2 dropped that restriction.
verification_note: LLaMA weights were gated: case-by-case research access under a noncommercial license (they later leaked).

name: GPT-4
notable_for: GPT-4, released by OpenAI in March 2023, was the first GPT model to accept image inputs; OpenAI did not disclose its parameter count. Users could show it photos or charts and ask questions in text. Withholding size and training details broke with earlier GPT papers, which had published both.

name: Claude
notable_for: Anthropic's first Claude model was released by invitation in March 2023 and used Constitutional AI. Constitutional AI trains models to critique and revise their own answers against a written list of principles, reducing how much human rating is needed. It was Anthropic's entry into assistant products four months after ChatGPT.

name: PaLM 2
notable_for: PaLM 2, released by Google in May 2023, is a family of language models noted for multilingual, reasoning, and coding capabilities. It was trained on almost five times as much text as the first PaLM of 2022, following the industry shift toward more data per parameter. Google used it to power 25 features and products, including its Bard chatbot.

name: Llama 2
notable_for: Llama 2, released by Meta in July 2023, is a family of pretrained and fine-tuned language models from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters, with Llama 2-Chat optimized for dialogue. Unlike LLaMA five months earlier, its weights came with a license permitting commercial use. Mistral 7B and Qwen-72B followed with open weights within four months.

name: Claude 2
notable_for: Claude 2, from Anthropic in July 2023, supports 100K-token prompts and can generate longer responses. Tokens are word fragments, so 100K tokens is roughly 75,000 words, enough to paste in one whole book and ask about it. Claude 2 was offered publicly in the US and UK through claude.ai's beta, where Claude four months earlier had been by invitation.

name: Falcon 180B
notable_for: Falcon 180B, from Abu Dhabi's Technology Innovation Institute (TII) in September 2023, is an openly available 180-billion-parameter language model trained on 3.5 trillion tokens. Tokens are word fragments read in training. Hugging Face's release post called it the largest openly available language model, 2.5 times the size of Llama 2, and noted that its license allowed commercial use only under restrictive conditions.

name: Mistral 7B
notable_for: Mistral 7B, released in September 2023, is a 7.3-billion-parameter model released under Apache 2.0 that outperforms Llama 2 13B on the benchmarks reported by Mistral AI. Apache 2.0 is a permissive license that allows commercial use; benchmarks are standardized tests. Mistral's point was that its 7.3-billion model beat one of 13 billion on those tests.

name: Qwen-72B
notable_for: Qwen-72B is a 72-billion-parameter open-weight model that extended the first Qwen generation, released by Alibaba Cloud on November 30, 2023. Open weight means trained model files can be downloaded and run. At 72 billion parameters it slightly exceeded Llama 2's largest 70-billion version.

name: Mixtral 8x7B
notable_for: Mixtral 8x7B, released by Mistral AI in December 2023, is an open-weights sparse mixture-of-experts language model with 46.7 billion total parameters and 12.9 billion active per token. Mixture-of-experts divides its network into eight expert blocks and routes each word fragment to two of them, so it runs at the cost of a 13-billion model while storing 46.7 billion parameters. It shipped under Apache 2.0 with a 32,768-token context window, and DBRX, Grok-1 and DeepSeek-V2, all mixture-of-experts models, followed within five months.

name: Gemini 1.0 Ultra
notable_for: Gemini 1.0 Ultra, announced by Google DeepMind in December 2023, was Google's largest and most capable Gemini model, designed for highly complex tasks. Google reported it exceeding state-of-the-art results on 30 of 32 widely used benchmarks, meaning best prior published scores on standardized tests. Google says Gemini was built to be multimodal from the ground up across text, audio, image and video, rather than adding image handling to text models.

name: Gemma
notable_for: Gemma, from Google in February 2024, is a family of lightweight open models released in 2B and 7B sizes, built using research and technology from Gemini models. Open means trained files can be downloaded and run locally. It arrived as Llama 2 and Mistral 7B spread.

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
notable_for: Gemini 1.5 Pro, from Google DeepMind in February 2024, introduced an experimental context window of up to 1 million tokens and can reason across text, images, audio, and video. Context window means how much material it can take in at once; 1 million tokens is roughly 700,000 words, or one hour of video. Its standard window was 128,000 tokens; its million-token version went to a limited group.

name: Grok-1
notable_for: Grok-1, released by xAI in March 2024, is a 314-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model released as base weights under the Apache 2.0 license. Mixture-of-experts means only part of its network runs for each word fragment; base weights means raw pretrained files without chat tuning.

name: Claude 3 Opus
notable_for: Anthropic described Claude 3 Opus, released in March 2024, as its most intelligent model, with strong performance across common AI benchmarks. It also processes images as well as text. Benchmarks are standardized tests, and Anthropic reported Opus outperforming its peers on most common ones; Opus was the largest of three tiers, above Sonnet and Haiku.

name: DBRX
notable_for: DBRX, from Databricks in March 2024, is a fine-grained mixture-of-experts language model with 132 billion total parameters and 36 billion active for any input. Fine-grained means it uses 16 smaller experts and picks four per word fragment, rather than Mixtral's eight experts with two chosen. Databricks released its weights openly and called it a new state-of-the-art open LLM.

name: Llama 3 70B
notable_for: Llama 3 70B, from Meta in April 2024, is a 70-billion-parameter language model that is instruction-tuned for dialogue and assistant-style interactions. Instruction-tuned means the base model was further trained on examples of following requests. It was pretrained on over 15 trillion tokens, a dataset seven times larger than Llama 2's, and its weights are open to download.

name: Phi-3-mini
notable_for: Phi-3-mini, from Microsoft in April 2024, is a lightweight 3.8-billion-parameter language model designed to run locally on a phone. Microsoft reported performance rivaling much larger models such as Mixtral 8x7B and GPT-3.5. It was trained on heavily filtered web data and synthetic data rather than raw web text, and Microsoft argued that data quality could substitute for size.

name: GPT-4o
notable_for: GPT-4o, from OpenAI in May 2024, processes text, audio, images, and video and can respond across modalities live. ChatGPT's earlier voice mode chained separate speech-to-text, language and text-to-speech models; GPT-4o handles sound and images in one network, so it can answer spoken questions with a human-like delay. OpenAI made it available to free ChatGPT users.

name: DeepSeek-V2
notable_for: DeepSeek-V2, from DeepSeek in May 2024, is a 236-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model that activates 21 billion parameters per token and uses Multi-head Latent Attention to reduce KV-cache size. Mixture-of-experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment; its KV cache is working memory that grows as conversations lengthen, and compressing it cuts serving cost. DeepSeek offered it through an API at what it called an unbeatable price, with open weights.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
notable_for: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, from Anthropic in June 2024, outperformed Claude 3 Opus on many evaluations while operating at twice its speed. Sonnet was Anthropic's mid-size tier, so its mid-size model beat its top model released three months earlier. It also introduced Artifacts, a side panel showing code or documents it produces.

name: Nemotron-4 340B
notable_for: Nemotron-4 340B, from NVIDIA in June 2024, is a 340-billion-parameter open model whose base, instruct, and reward models form an open pipeline for generating synthetic data. Synthetic data is training text written by models instead of people, used to train and refine language models; its reward model scores that text so only good examples are kept. NVIDIA offered it as a free way for developers to generate training data for their own language models.

name: Llama 3.1 405B
notable_for: Llama 3.1 405B, from Meta in July 2024, is an openly available 405-billion-parameter model with capabilities in general knowledge, math, tool use, and multilingual translation. Openly available means trained files can be downloaded. Meta called it the first frontier-level open source model and said it was competitive with leading closed models including GPT-4.

name: Mistral Large 2
notable_for: Mistral Large 2, from Mistral AI in July 2024, has 123 billion parameters and a 128k-token context window and is designed for strong multilingual, code-generation, mathematics, and reasoning performance. Context window means how much text it can consider at once; 128k tokens is roughly 95,000 words. Released July 24, 2024 under the Mistral Research License, its weights could be used and modified for research and non-commercial purposes.

name: FLUX.1
notable_for: FLUX.1, from Black Forest Labs in August 2024, is a 12-billion-parameter text-to-image model family with open-weight dev and schnell variants. Black Forest Labs was founded by Stable Diffusion's original creators; dev is its full-quality version and schnell its version tuned for speed, and both can be downloaded and run locally. Black Forest Labs raised $31 million at launch.

name: OpenAI o1
notable_for: OpenAI o1, released in September 2024, is trained with reinforcement learning to spend more time reasoning through complex problems before responding. Reinforcement learning rewards the model for chains of steps that reach correct answers, so it learns to write out working before giving a final reply. DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Gemini 2.5 Pro, all reasoning models, followed within six months.

name: Qwen2.5-72B
notable_for: Qwen2.5-72B, from Alibaba's Qwen team in September 2024, is a 72.7-billion-parameter open-weights language model with multilingual capabilities and strong coding and mathematics performance. It supports context lengths up to 128,000 tokens, roughly 95,000 words of input; open weights means downloadable model files. It was pretrained on 18 trillion tokens and supports over 29 languages.

name: Sora
notable_for: Sora, released by OpenAI in December 2024, generates videos from text prompts or images and can extend, remix, and blend videos. OpenAI had previewed it in February 2024; the public release came ten months later with clips up to 20 seconds. Users could generate at up to 1080p resolution.

name: Veo 2
notable_for: Veo 2, from Google DeepMind in December 2024, generates realistic videos with improved understanding of physics and cinematic camera controls, at resolutions up to 4K. Camera controls let prompts ask for specific lenses or movements. It arrived in the same month as OpenAI's Sora.

name: DeepSeek-V3
notable_for: DeepSeek-V3, from DeepSeek in December 2024, is a 671-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model with 37 billion parameters activated per token. Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs for each word fragment, so it costs about as much to run as a 37-billion model. It was trained on 14.8 trillion tokens of text, and its weights and papers were released openly.

name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
notable_for: Gemini 2.0 Flash, from Google DeepMind in December 2024, supports multimodal inputs and outputs, including image and audio generation. It can natively use tools such as Google Search and code execution, meaning it decides on its own when to search or run code rather than relying on a separate program. Flash is Google's mid-size tier, built for speed.

name: DeepSeek-R1
notable_for: DeepSeek-R1, released in January 2025 under an MIT license, is a 671-billion-parameter reasoning model that DeepSeek claims performs on par with OpenAI o1 on certain benchmarks. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; MIT licensing lets anyone use its weights for any purpose. DeepSeek's claim was that an open model had matched o1 nine months after o1's release.

name: o3-mini
notable_for: o3-mini, from OpenAI in January 2025, is a cost-efficient reasoning model optimized for science, math, and coding, with adjustable reasoning effort. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; adjustable effort lets users pick low, medium or high amounts of that step-writing. It was released in the same month as DeepSeek-R1 and was the first reasoning model offered to free ChatGPT users.

name: Grok 3
notable_for: Grok 3, released by xAI in February 2025, is a family of models with reasoning variants, and xAI claims it outperforms GPT-4o on some benchmarks. Reasoning variants write out steps before answering; benchmarks are standard tests. It was trained in a Memphis data center containing around 200,000 GPUs, or graphics chips.

name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
notable_for: Claude 3.7 Sonnet, from Anthropic in February 2025, is a hybrid reasoning model that can answer in one pass or with extended step-by-step thinking. Anthropic reported particular improvements in coding and web development. Hybrid means one model offers both modes, and users set how many tokens it may spend thinking; it shipped with Claude Code, Anthropic's command-line coding agent.

name: GPT-4.5
notable_for: GPT-4.5, released by OpenAI in February 2025, was OpenAI's largest chat model at launch, designed for more natural conversations, broader knowledge, and fewer hallucinations. Hallucinations are confident but false statements. OpenAI presented it as a step up in scaling ordinary pretraining, as distinct from its reasoning models, and said at launch it was evaluating whether to keep serving it in its API long-term.

name: Gemma 3
notable_for: Gemma 3, from Google in March 2025, is an open-weight model family available in sizes from 1B to 27B, with image understanding and support for over 140 languages. Context windows reach 128K tokens; open weight means downloadable model files, and 1B to 27B is parameter count in billions. Its 27B model ran on one GPU while scoring near much larger models on human-preference rankings.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
notable_for: Gemini 2.5 Pro, from Google DeepMind in March 2025, is a thinking model noted for advanced reasoning and coding capabilities, a one-million-token context window, and strong benchmark results. Thinking model means it writes out steps before answering; context window means how much material it can take in at once. It debuted at number one on LMArena's human-preference leaderboard.

name: Llama 4 Maverick
notable_for: Llama 4 Maverick, from Meta in April 2025, is a 17 billion active parameter mixture-of-experts model with 128 experts and 400 billion total parameters. Mixture-of-experts means each word fragment is handled by one of 128 expert blocks plus one shared block, so only 17 billion parameters do work at any moment. Meta called it natively multimodal, taking images as well as text, and its LMArena score of 1417 came from an experimental chat version rather than its released weights.

name: o3
notable_for: o3, from OpenAI in April 2025, is a reasoning model known for strong performance in coding, math, science, and visual perception. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; o3 could also call tools such as web search and Python while thinking. It can also bring images into its chain of thought, rotating or zooming them as part of its work.

name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
notable_for: Qwen3-235B-A22B, from Alibaba in April 2025, is a flagship Mixture-of-Experts model with 235 billion total parameters and 22 billion active per inference step. Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs for each word fragment, which is what A22B in its name records. Its weights are open to download, and its thinking variant writes out steps before answering.

name: Claude Opus 4
notable_for: Claude Opus 4, from Anthropic in May 2025, is designed for coding, advanced reasoning, and long-running agent workflows. Agent workflow means it works through a multi-step task on its own, using software tools, rather than answering one question at a time. Anthropic shipped it with measures for higher AI Safety Levels such as ASL-3, its internal scale of safeguards.

name: Veo 3
notable_for: Veo 3, from Google DeepMind in May 2025, generates video with synchronized audio, including dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise. Sora and Veo 2, five months earlier, generated video without sound; Google presented synchronized audio as Veo 3's new ability.

name: Magistral
notable_for: Magistral, from Mistral AI in June 2025, is Mistral AI's first reasoning model, released in an open 24B Small variant and a proprietary Medium variant. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; 24B means 24 billion parameters, and Small's weights are downloadable. It came nine months after OpenAI o1.

name: Kimi K2
notable_for: Kimi K2, from Moonshot AI in July 2025, is an open-weight mixture-of-experts model with about 1 trillion total parameters known for coding and agentic capabilities. Mixture-of-experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment; agentic means it can carry out multi-step tasks using tools. Moonshot published its weights for download.

name: Grok 4
notable_for: Grok 4, from xAI in July 2025, is a flagship reasoning model with native tool use and live search integration. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; native tool use means it decides on its own when to run code or search the web, including live posts on X. It followed Grok 3 by five months.

name: GLM-4.5
notable_for: GLM-4.5, from Zhipu AI (Z.ai) in July 2025, is a 355-billion-parameter open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model that combines reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities. Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment; agentic means it can carry out multi-step tasks with tools. It was one of several Chinese open models released that summer, alongside Kimi K2.

name: gpt-oss-120b
notable_for: gpt-oss-120b, released by OpenAI in August 2025, is an open-weight mixture-of-experts reasoning model with 117 billion parameters and strong tool-use capabilities that fits on a single 80 GB GPU. Open weight means downloadable model files; OpenAI called it its first open-weight language model since GPT-2 in 2019. One 80 GB GPU is one high-end graphics chip, so companies could run it on their own hardware.

name: GPT-5
notable_for: GPT-5, released by OpenAI in August 2025, is a unified system that routes between immediate responses and deeper reasoning. OpenAI reported strong performance in coding, math, writing, health, and visual perception. Routing means one controller decides, per request, whether to answer at once or switch to slower step-by-step mode; GPT-5 replaced GPT-4o and OpenAI's o-series models in ChatGPT.

name: Genie 3
notable_for: Genie 3, from Google DeepMind in August 2025, generates live interactive worlds from text prompts at 720p and 24 frames per second, maintaining consistency for a few minutes. World models produce each new frame in response to users' moves, like video games drawn on demand instead of from pre-built scenery. DeepMind presented it as training space for robots and other agents.

name: Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana)
notable_for: Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, nicknamed Nano Banana, from Google DeepMind in August 2025, generates and edits images from natural-language instructions. It can blend multiple images, maintain character consistency, and make targeted changes; character consistency means one person or object keeps its look across many generated pictures. Flash is Google's mid-size tier, built for speed and low cost.

name: Qwen3-Max
notable_for: Qwen3-Max, from Alibaba in September 2025, is Alibaba's largest Qwen model, with over one trillion parameters, and is notable for its coding and autonomous agent capabilities. Unlike earlier Qwen releases its weights were not published. Autonomous agent capability means it can carry out multi-step tasks with software tools on its own.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
notable_for: Claude Sonnet 4.5, from Anthropic in September 2025, is designed for complex agents, coding, computer use, reasoning, and math. Computer use means it operates a screen, clicking and typing in ordinary software. Anthropic reported it working on its own for more than 30 hours on a coding task.

name: Sora 2
notable_for: Sora 2, from OpenAI in September 2025, generates realistic videos with synchronized dialogue and sound effects and improved physical accuracy and controllability. Physical accuracy means objects move and collide as they would in life. It launched inside a Sora app whose characters feature let users drop themselves into any generated scene.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp
notable_for: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, from DeepSeek-AI in September 2025 with 685 billion parameters and open weights, introduces DeepSeek Sparse Attention to improve training and inference efficiency on long-context tasks. DeepSeek reported comparable output quality. Attention is where every word fragment is compared with all others; sparse attention skips most of those comparisons, so long documents cost far less to process, and Exp marks it as an experimental step toward DeepSeek-V3.2 three months later.

name: MiniMax-M2
notable_for: MiniMax-M2, from MiniMax in October 2025, is an efficient Mixture-of-Experts model with 230 billion total parameters, of which 10 billion are active, designed for coding and agentic workflows. Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment; agentic means multi-step work with tools. Its weights are open.

name: Kimi K2 Thinking
notable_for: Kimi K2 Thinking, from Moonshot AI in November 2025, is an open-weight reasoning model of about 1 trillion parameters designed to use tools during long-running agentic tasks. Reasoning models write out steps before answering; here it keeps tool use stable across 200 to 300 sequential calls. Published benchmarks show it beating GPT-5 on agentic reasoning and agentic search.

name: Gemini 3 Pro
notable_for: Gemini 3 Pro, from Google DeepMind in November 2025, is a natively multimodal reasoning model designed for complex tasks and advanced agentic coding. Natively multimodal means one network was trained on text, audio, images and video together rather than combined from separate models; reasoning models write out steps before answering. Its model card lists Google Antigravity among its distribution channels.

name: Claude Opus 4.5
notable_for: Claude Opus 4.5, from Anthropic in November 2025, is designed for coding, agents, computer use, and enterprise workflows. Computer use means it operates ordinary software through the screen. Anthropic set its price at $5/$25 per million tokens.

name: GPT-5.2
notable_for: GPT-5.2, from OpenAI in December 2025, is designed for professional knowledge work, with improvements in long-context understanding, vision, tool use, and complex multi-step tasks. Long context means holding many documents in view at once. It followed GPT-5 by four months.

name: Mistral Large 3
notable_for: Mistral Large 3, from Mistral AI in December 2025, is an open-weight multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 41 billion active parameters and 675 billion total parameters. Multimodal means it takes images as well as text; Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment. Its weights were published for download.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2
notable_for: DeepSeek-V3.2, from DeepSeek in December 2025 with 685 billion parameters and open weights, integrates reasoning into tool use and uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention for efficient long-context processing. Reasoning into tool use means it keeps thinking step by step while calling search or code tools, instead of stopping to reason before each call. Sparse attention skips most word-to-word comparisons, so long documents cost less to process.

name: Claude Opus 4.6
notable_for: Claude Opus 4.6, from Anthropic in February 2026, improves coding, planning, code review, and debugging, and offers a 1M-token context window in beta. Context window means how much material it can take in at once; 1M tokens is roughly 700,000 words. Claude 2, in 2023, had offered 100K.

name: GLM-5
notable_for: GLM-5, from Zhipu AI in February 2026, is a 744-billion-parameter open-weight model designed for complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. Long-horizon agentic tasks are jobs that run for hours across many tool calls. Its weights are downloadable from Hugging Face.

name: Qwen3.5
notable_for: Qwen3.5, from Alibaba in February 2026, is an open-weight family whose flagship combines native vision-language capabilities with a hybrid architecture. That design activates 17 billion of its 397 billion parameters per forward pass, one run of its network producing one word fragment, so only 17 billion parameters do work at any moment. Native vision-language means images and text were trained together from day one.

name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
notable_for: Gemini 3.1 Pro, from Google DeepMind in February 2026, is designed for complex problem-solving and achieved a verified 77.1% score on the ARC-AGI-2 benchmark. ARC-AGI-2 tests novel visual puzzles built to resist memorization, on which humans had scored far higher than models. Verified means ARC Prize, which runs that benchmark, confirmed Google's result.

name: Seedance 2.0
notable_for: Seedance 2.0, ByteDance's multimodal video generator released in February 2026, drew Hollywood copyright complaints. Multimodal means it builds video from text, image, audio and video inputs together. Disney and Paramount Skydance sent cease-and-desist letters, and the Motion Picture Association said ByteDance had used copyrighted works on a massive scale; ByteDance said it would strengthen safeguards.

name: GPT-5.4
notable_for: GPT-5.4, from OpenAI in March 2026, combines reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows, with native computer-use capabilities and support for up to 1 million tokens of context. Computer use means it operates ordinary software through the screen; 1 million tokens is roughly 700,000 words of input. It matched Gemini's million-token length, which Google had offered since 2024.

name: Gemma 4
notable_for: Gemma 4, from Google in April 2026, is an open model family spanning edge, dense, and Mixture-of-Experts variants designed for complex reasoning and agentic workflows. Edge models are small enough to run on phones; dense models use all parameters per word fragment; Mixture-of-Experts models use only part. Its weights are downloadable, continuing the open line Google began with Gemma in 2024.

name: Claude Mythos Preview
notable_for: Claude Mythos Preview, from Anthropic in April 2026, is an advanced model focused on cybersecurity, software coding, and complex reasoning, including identifying vulnerabilities in large codebases. Vulnerabilities are flaws attackers can exploit. Amazon offered it through Bedrock as a gated research preview, with access limited to an initial allow-list of organizations, since finding flaws can serve attackers too.

name: GPT-5.5
notable_for: GPT-5.5, from OpenAI in April 2026, is designed for complex, multi-step work, including agentic coding, research, data analysis, and operating software across tools. Agentic coding means it writes and runs code over many steps on its own. It arrived one month after GPT-5.4.

name: Muse Spark
modality: voice, text, and image input; text output
notable_for: Muse Spark, from Meta in April 2026, is Meta Superintelligence Labs' first Muse model, built for multimodal reasoning, tool use, and multi-agent orchestration. Multi-agent orchestration means one model directs several copies working on parts of a task. Unlike Meta's Llama models, whose weights were downloadable, its weights were not published.

name: DeepSeek-V4
notable_for: DeepSeek-V4, from DeepSeek in April 2026, is an open-weight model family known for its 1-million-token context window; its Pro variant has 1.6 trillion total parameters. Context window means how much text it can take in at once; 1 million tokens is roughly 700,000 words. Open weight means trained files can be downloaded and run.

name: Gemini 3.5
notable_for: Gemini 3.5, from Google DeepMind in May 2026, is a family of models combining frontier intelligence with action, with a focus on agentic workflows and coding. Agentic workflows mean it carries out multi-step tasks with tools on its own. It arrived three months after Gemini 3.1 Pro.

name: Claude Fable 5
notable_for: Claude Fable 5, launched by Anthropic on June 9, 2026, is described by Anthropic as a Mythos-class model made safe for general use. Claude Mythos 5 is its same underlying model with fewer safeguards for vetted partners; both cost $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. Anthropic's example of its reach: migrating a 50-million-line Ruby codebase in one day, work it says would have taken one team over two months.

name: Claude Opus 5
notable_for: Claude Opus 5, released by Anthropic on July 24, 2026, performs strongly on coding and knowledge work evaluations and is priced at half of Claude Fable 5. It costs $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, and Anthropic describes it as coming close to Fable 5's capability at that lower price. Evaluations here are standardized tests such as Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA.

name: Kimi K3
notable_for: Kimi K3, from Moonshot AI in July 2026, is a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight multimodal model with a 1-million-token context window. Open weight means trained files can be downloaded; multimodal means it takes images as well as text; 1 million tokens is roughly 700,000 words of input. Its 2.8 trillion parameters were more than twice Kimi K2's 1 trillion.

name: GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, Luna)
notable_for: GPT-5.6, OpenAI's three-tier model family, was made generally available on July 9, 2026. Sol is its flagship, Terra is described as balanced for everyday work, and Luna as most cost-efficient. OpenAI priced them per million tokens at $5 input and $30 output for Sol, $2.50 and $15 for Terra, and $1 and $6 for Luna.

name: Inkling
notable_for: Inkling, released on July 15, 2026, is the first open-weight model from Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab. It is a Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975 billion total and 41 billion active parameters, pretrained on 45 trillion tokens, with a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Mixture-of-Experts means only part of its network runs per word fragment; open weight means trained files can be downloaded and fine-tuned.
verification_note: The launch page reports 975B total and 41B active parameters, training on text, images, audio and video, and weights on Hugging Face.

name: Claude Opus 5.5
notable_for: Claude Opus 5.5, from Anthropic in September 2026, is built for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. Agentic coding means it writes, runs and fixes code over many steps without a person directing each one. It followed Claude Opus 5 by two months.

name: Gemini 4 Argon
notable_for: Gemini 4 Argon, from Google DeepMind in September 2026, is built for complex, long-horizon work in software engineering, finance, legal tasks, and cybersecurity. It can process documents containing text, tables, charts, and images. Long-horizon work means tasks that run for hours across many steps; it was released in the same month as OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.

name: GPT-6 Astra
notable_for: GPT-6 Astra, released by OpenAI in September 2026, is the first OpenAI model rated Critical for cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework. The framework is OpenAI's internal scale for dangerous capabilities, and Critical is its highest tier. OpenAI called it the most capable model it had broadly deployed and reported that, across more than 54,000 internal Codex tasks, it received roughly half as many flags for higher-severity misaligned behavior as GPT-5.6 Sol.

name: Muse Spark Open
notable_for: Muse Spark Open, from Meta in October 2026, is an open-weight coding and agentic model with 816 billion total and 42 billion active parameters. Open weight means trained files can be downloaded; active parameters are the share that runs for each word fragment. It restored open releases at Meta six months after the closed Muse Spark.
verification_note: The launch page reports 816B total and 42B active parameters, released weights, and a natively multimodal design.

name: Mistral Large 4
notable_for: Mistral Large 4, Mistral AI's flagship model, was released in public preview on October 6, 2026. Mistral describes it as a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters, built as an open-weight hybrid that can answer directly or reason step by step, with weights promised by the end of October. It is priced at $0.7 per million input tokens and $2.1 per million output tokens.

name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
notable_for: Kimi K3.1 Pro, from Moonshot AI in October 2026, is a post-trained Kimi K3 with 2.8 trillion total and 104 billion active parameters, image input and a 1-million-token context. Open weights were promised by November 4, 2026. Post-trained means July's base model was given further training rather than built anew; active parameters are those that run per word fragment.

name: Dessa
notable_for: Dessa, from Block in October 2026, is a full-duplex speech-to-speech research preview trained from scratch on human conversation with no text, on a single GB200 NVL72. It runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max. Full-duplex means it listens and talks at once, like someone who can be interrupted; one GB200 NVL72 is one NVIDIA rack-scale computing system, and running on one laptop means no data center is needed.
